questions.q: A researcher skims an archive for the famous documents and skips boxes of routine correspondence. What would Caro say?
choices: Turn every page: the crucial document is usually buried in routine material
Start with the resolution and work backward
Focus on the documents that confirm your thesis
Archives are less reliable than interviews
questions.explain: Caro credits the advice to his Newsday editor Alan Hathway.

questions.q: During an interview, a subject pauses. What does Caro's 'SU' remind him to do?
choices: Summarize what the subject has said
Shut up and let the silence run, because people often fill it with what they hadn't planned to say
Switch to a new topic
Show the subject a document
questions.explain: He writes SU in his notebook to stop himself filling silences.

questions.q: Why did Caro move to the Texas Hill Country?
choices: To find Johnson's private papers
Because Johnson's family invited him
He realized he didn't understand the people there, and so didn't understand Johnson; living there let him make readers see the place
To write a novel set there
questions.explain: He moved with his wife Ina in 1978 and lived there for much of the next three years.

questions.q: What does Caro insist on knowing before he begins writing a book?
choices: The first sentence
The title
The publication date
The ending, down to the last sentence, with a full outline
questions.explain: Knowing the end tells him what every chapter builds toward; compare Franklin's 'find the resolution first'.

questions.q: In 'One Mile', Caro follows a single mile of the Cross-Bronx Expressway through East Tremont. What is the technique?
choices: Showing abstract power through particular people and places where it lands
Opening with an anecdote, then a nut graf
Cross-cutting two timelines
Using a composite character
questions.explain: His books are about how power works, shown at ground level.

questions.q: Which is a well-known dispute about The Power Broker?
choices: Whether Moses existed
Whether Moses built low parkway overpasses deliberately to keep buses off; later researchers say the evidence for that intent is thin
Whether Caro interviewed anyone
Whether Gottlieb edited it
questions.explain: The low-bridges claim is famous and contested.

questions.q: A screenwriter is writing a film about a real trial. What would Caro's method suggest?
choices: Rely on the famous testimony everyone quotes
Invent dialogue for drama first and check facts later
Read the whole transcript, visit the places, and know the final image before drafting
Keep research light so it doesn't slow the writing
questions.explain: Deep research, sense of place and knowing the ending first.

ideas: Turn every page: never assume you know what a file contains.
Write 'SU' in your notebook during interviews to remind yourself to let silences run.
Move to the place where your subject grew up and spend a night alone there, because the reader can't see what you haven't seen.
Power doesn't always corrupt, but it always reveals who someone is.
